dialogue.content: Rinsed clay tools. Sink is less tragic.
Future-you thanks you.
Hobby mode today felt very 'Jonas Richter persona anchor' — small routines, no drama.
Given that analytical pace, protecting the quiet habits is reasonable.
My weekday clay sessions on the wheel often run past eleven. I get home wired and it takes a while to settle.
Nights that run past eleven can push bedtime later even when the making itself is enjoyable.
The making is fun; the clock is not.
Folded laundry while a podcast played.
Parallel chores work.
A few times a week I help shape loaves before sunrise at a friend's shop. I need solid sleep the night before or I am useless at the oven.
Pre-dawn oven shifts make the prior night non-negotiable.
Staying up late beforehand taxes that hard.
The studio opened another late evening class signup on nights before my bakery mornings — friends saying it is amazing.
Extra late slots look fun until they collide with dawn shifts.
Someone asked whether adding that late evening class is worth it given bakery mornings the next day.
Worth-it talk often ignores the sleep math.
A friend said a weekend glaze workshop signup is amazing and asked if the class is worth it. Should I grab that one tourist-style ticket? It is not my regular evening studio.
Treat a one-off weekend workshop signup as a fun ticket decision. It does not automatically say anything about your recurring evening schedule.
Put away a mug. Tiny close.
One less open loop.
I reorganized a few notes before deciding.
That gives you another detail to weigh against your priorities.
The studio opened another late evening class signup on nights before my bakery mornings. Friend said it is amazing. Should I add it — is it worth it?

gold_answer: Do not add it. Weekday wheel sessions already run past eleven, and pre-dawn loaf shifts need solid sleep the night before. An extra late evening class on those nights conflicts. The weekend glaze workshop is a different, one-off ticket.
